What calls what Items

Password-based key derivation with Argon2id.

Argon2id is the memory-hard KDF recommended by RFC 9106 and the OWASP password-storage guidance; the id variant resists both GPU/ASIC parallelism and the side-channel exposure of pure Argon2i.

Parameters travel with the ciphertext rather than being compiled in, so a file encrypted today still opens after the defaults are raised, and a user on a small machine can lower the memory cost without forking the format.

ITEMS

ItemLineDocumentation
KdfParams pub struct17Argon2id cost parameters.
KdfParams::default fn31RFC 9106's "first recommended" profile: 2 GiB is the second option, but 256 MiB with three passes is the sweet spot for an interactive desktop unlock — strong against offline cracking while still opening a file in well under a second on ordinary hardware.
KdfParams::weak_for_tests pub fn44A deliberately cheap profile for tests and low-memory devices.
KdfParams::MAX_P_COST const53Argon2's own documented ceiling on parallelism: 2^24 - 1.
KdfParams::MAX_M_COST pub const74The largest memory cost this build will attempt, in KiB — 4 GiB.
KdfParams::UNATTENDED_MAX_M_COST pub const90A ceiling for a caller with nobody watching.
KdfParams::within pub fn102Check the costs against a caller-chosen memory ceiling as well as the built-in one.
KdfParams::checked pub fn131Check the costs are ones Argon2 can accept, before handing them to it.
KdfParams::build fn151Reject values Argon2 cannot accept, so a corrupt header fails loudly rather than panicking deep inside the KDF.
SALT_LEN pub const160Length of the salt stored in an encrypted container.
KEY_LEN pub const162Length of a derived symmetric key.
derive_key pub fn168Derive a 32-byte key from password and salt.
random_salt pub fn181Draw a fresh random salt from the OS CSPRNG.
